title: Deep learning epitope-processing escapes associate with survival in NSCLC immunotherapy
summary: Whole-exome data of 400 NSCLC patients from TCGA and an immune checkpoint cohort of 48 nivolumab-treated primary tumors were analyzed. A deep learning method trained on 1,260 known MHC-I ligands evaluated how mutations affect proteasomal processing of epitopes. Processing escapes were associated with decreased overall survival in TCGA (p = 0.0140), and in the checkpoint cohort patients with escapes plus high PD-L1 (8/48) had significantly decreased overall survival independent of mutational load or PD-L1 status. The checkpoint subgroup is very small and the analysis is retrospective.
